title: Hybrid RAG fixture benchmark v1
description: A fixed offline benchmark over the repository fixture corpus. It pins a graph-independent corpus content hash, balances fact, comparison, relation, and cross-document questions, and anchors every score in verbatim source text.

cases.question: What does naive retrieval-augmented generation usually retrieve?

expected_evidence.text: Naive retrieval-augmented generation usually retrieves isolated text chunks.

cases.reference_answer: Naive retrieval-augmented generation usually retrieves isolated text chunks.

cases.question: What additional route to evidence does the graph provide?

expected_evidence.text: The graph provides an additional route to evidence while the original chunks remain the source of truth.

cases.reference_answer: The graph provides an additional route to evidence while original chunks remain the source of truth.

cases.question: Where does local retrieval start?

expected_evidence.text: Local retrieval starts from concrete entities and expands their nearby relations.

cases.reference_answer: Local retrieval starts from concrete entities and expands nearby relations.

cases.question: What signals does global retrieval start from?

expected_evidence.text: Global retrieval starts from higher-level relation or topic signals.

cases.reference_answer: Global retrieval starts from higher-level relation or topic signals.

cases.question: Which graph routes does hybrid retrieval combine?

expected_evidence.text: Hybrid retrieval combines the local entity-led and global relation-led graph routes.

cases.reference_answer: Hybrid retrieval combines the local entity-led and global relation-led graph routes.

cases.question: What should every chunk point back to for source tracing?

expected_evidence.text: Every chunk should point back to its document and a page range or character span.

cases.reference_answer: Every chunk should point back to its document and a page range or character span.

cases.question: How do naive retrieval and a LightRAG-style graph differ for relationships spanning sources?

expected_evidence.text: This is useful for local facts, but it can lose relationships that span documents or sections.
The graph provides an additional route to evidence while the original chunks remain the source of truth.

cases.reference_answer: Naive retrieval can lose relationships across documents or sections, while the graph adds an evidence route without replacing source chunks.

cases.question: How do local and global retrieval differ in their starting signals?

expected_evidence.text: Local retrieval starts from concrete entities and expands their nearby relations.
Global retrieval starts from higher-level relation or topic signals.

cases.reference_answer: Local starts from concrete entities and nearby relations; global starts from higher-level relation or topic signals.

cases.question: Which retrieval mode is suited to named entities, and which is suited to summaries and comparisons?

expected_evidence.text: It is suitable for questions about a named method, dataset, metric, or author.
It is suitable for summary and comparison questions that require evidence from several parts of a corpus.

cases.reference_answer: Local retrieval suits questions about named methods, datasets, metrics, or authors; global retrieval suits summary and comparison questions across corpus parts.

cases.question: How does hybrid retrieval differ from a naive chunk-only approach?

expected_evidence.text: Naive retrieval-augmented generation usually retrieves isolated text chunks.
Hybrid retrieval combines the local entity-led and global relation-led graph routes.

cases.reference_answer: Naive retrieval uses isolated chunks, whereas hybrid combines the local entity-led and global relation-led graph routes.

cases.question: What distinction does retrieval-augmented generation make between external knowledge and model parameters?

expected_evidence.text: Retrieval-augmented generation separates external knowledge from model parameters.

cases.reference_answer: Retrieval-augmented generation separates external knowledge from model parameters.

cases.question: Which processing inputs must remain the same for deterministic ingestion identifiers?

expected_evidence.text: The same source, parser version, cleaner version, tokenizer, and chunking configuration should generate the same identifiers.

cases.reference_answer: The source, parser and cleaner versions, tokenizer, and chunking configuration must remain the same.

cases.question: What does a LightRAG-style system extract before retrieval?

expected_evidence.text: LightRAG-style systems extract entities and relations before retrieval.

cases.reference_answer: It extracts entities and relations before retrieval.

cases.question: What is the relationship between graph evidence and original chunks?

expected_evidence.text: The graph provides an additional route to evidence while the original chunks remain the source of truth.

cases.reference_answer: The graph provides an additional evidence route, but original chunks remain the source of truth.

cases.question: How are concrete entities related to nearby relations in local retrieval?

expected_evidence.text: Local retrieval starts from concrete entities and expands their nearby relations.

cases.reference_answer: Local retrieval starts from concrete entities and expands their nearby relations.

cases.question: How are higher-level signals related to evidence in global retrieval?

expected_evidence.text: Global retrieval starts from higher-level relation or topic signals.
It is suitable for summary and comparison questions that require evidence from several parts of a corpus.

cases.reference_answer: Global retrieval uses higher-level relation or topic signals and is suited to questions requiring evidence from several corpus parts.

cases.question: Why must retrieved context retain source identifiers?

expected_evidence.text: The final context must retain source identifiers so that an answer can cite its evidence.

cases.reference_answer: Source identifiers let the answer cite its evidence.

cases.question: Why is source tracing required for evaluation?

expected_evidence.text: Source tracing is required for evaluation.
Every chunk should point back to its document and a page range or character span.

cases.reference_answer: Source tracing is required for evaluation because chunks must point to their document and page range or character span.

cases.question: Across the notes, how do the retriever and generator work after external knowledge is separated from parameters?

expected_evidence.text: Retrieval-augmented generation separates external knowledge from model parameters.
A retriever selects evidence and a generator answers from that evidence.

cases.reference_answer: RAG separates external knowledge from parameters; the retriever selects evidence and the generator answers from it.

cases.question: How do deterministic ingestion and source tracing jointly support repeatable evaluation?

expected_evidence.text: The same source, parser version, cleaner version, tokenizer, and chunking configuration should generate the same identifiers.
Source tracing is required for evaluation.

cases.reference_answer: Stable processing inputs produce stable identifiers, while source tracing makes the resulting evidence auditable for evaluation.

cases.question: How can graph-assisted retrieval remain grounded and cite its evidence?

expected_evidence.text: The graph provides an additional route to evidence while the original chunks remain the source of truth.
The final context must retain source identifiers so that an answer can cite its evidence.

cases.reference_answer: The graph adds an evidence route while chunks remain authoritative, and retained source identifiers allow citations.

cases.question: Why might a summary question need global rather than naive retrieval?

expected_evidence.text: This is useful for local facts, but it can lose relationships that span documents or sections.
It is suitable for summary and comparison questions that require evidence from several parts of a corpus.

cases.reference_answer: Naive retrieval can lose cross-document relationships, whereas global retrieval is designed for summaries needing evidence from several corpus parts.

cases.question: How can local entity expansion contribute to hybrid retrieval?

expected_evidence.text: Local retrieval starts from concrete entities and expands their nearby relations.
Hybrid retrieval combines the local entity-led and global relation-led graph routes.

cases.reference_answer: Local retrieval contributes entity-led graph evidence, and hybrid combines it with the global relation-led route.

cases.question: How do chunks serve both generation and evaluation across the corpus?

expected_evidence.text: A retriever selects evidence and a generator answers from that evidence.
Every chunk should point back to its document and a page range or character span.

cases.reference_answer: Chunks provide evidence for generation and retain document and location provenance for evaluation.
